referenceAnswerText: When students begin a research project, they are often told to rely on primary texts rather than secondary sources. A primary text is an original document, such as a letter, a diary or a scientific report, written at the time of the events it describes. Secondary texts, by contrast, interpret or comment on those original materials. Both types are useful, but reading the primary material first allows students to form their own opinions before they are influenced by the views of other scholars.
